pages.text: A whole cut of meat is a meal for one. Held against an edge, it becomes a meal for several.$(br2)Meat in one hand, an edge in the other, $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact).
You are not the only one who will ever be hungry.$(br2)$(l)Remember who fed whom.$() Others will.

Everything that dies leaves a carcass where it fell, and things die out here without anyone's help - worn out, sick, or carrying an old wound. Break one for a rib, a long bone or a plain bone, and whatever meat is left on it.$(br2)Eat a rib and the bone stays in your hand. Crack it for the marrow.

Older bones lie scattered out in the country, picked clean long ago. They are rare, and worth the walk: three to five bones, two or three long bones, and a rib or two.$(br2)Meat on the ground carries a long way. A giant hyena may reach a fresh kill before you do, and it will take the lot - get there first, or frighten it off.

You are not the only one who lost a band. Now and then a carcass has somebody of your own kind sitting beside it, living off what they find - more often at old bone beds than fresh kills.$(br2)Nothing with a nose comes near a kill a hominin is sitting at. Walk up to them and they will get up and come with you.
